questions.question: In Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World, Russell Crowe plays Captain Jack Aubrey — which navy does he serve in?
questions.note: Set during the Napoleonic Wars and adapted from Patrick O'Brian's novels, it has Crowe's Royal Navy captain hunting the French privateer Acheron.

questions.question: Which lake is the largest in England?
questions.note: Windermere, in Cumbria's Lake District, is about 17 km long and covers roughly six square miles.

questions.question: This 1821 painting by John Constable — one of the best-loved of all British pictures — hangs in which London museum?
questions.imageAlt: A rural painting of a horse-drawn hay cart fording a shallow river beside a cottage
questions.imageCredit: The Hay Wain (1821), John Constable · Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
questions.note: It's The Hay Wain, catalogued as NG1207, on Trafalgar Square — and it was shown in Paris in 1824, where it made a deep impression on French painters.

questions.question: According to Law 1 of the Laws of Cricket, written by the MCC at Lord's, how many players are there in a cricket team?
questions.note: Law 1 states a match is played between two sides of eleven players each, one of whom is the captain.

questions.question: The Great Fire of London in 1666 broke out in a bakery on which street?
questions.note: The fire started in Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane on 2 September 1666 and burned for four days.

questions.question: The British spread Marmite takes its name from a French word for what kind of object?
questions.note: A marmite is a French earthenware or metal cooking pot, and the spread was originally sold in small pots of that shape.

questions.question: How many miles long is Hadrian's Wall, shown here, which crosses northern England coast to coast?
questions.imageAlt: A low stone wall running over rolling green hills under a wide sky
questions.imageCredit: Hadrian's Wall, Northumberland · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (credit at source)
questions.note: The Roman wall runs 73 modern miles — 80 Roman miles, about 117 km — from Wallsend to Bowness-on-Solway.

questions.question: Russell Crowe played Inspector Javert in the 2012 film Les Misérables — which French author wrote the 1862 novel behind it?
questions.note: Tom Hooper's film adapts the stage musical, which is itself based on Hugo's 1862 novel.

questions.question: The marathon distance of 26 miles 385 yards was fixed at the Olympic Games held in which city?
questions.note: The 1908 London Games ran from Windsor Castle to the stadium, and that length became the official marathon distance in 1921.

questions.question: Three of these British artists have won the Turner Prize. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: Hirst won in 1995, McQueen in 1999 and Perry in 2003. The anonymous street artist Banksy has never won the Tate's prize.

questions.question: In France, an estate agent tells you a flat is 'au premier étage'. Which floor is it on?
questions.answer: The floor above the ground floor
options: The floor above the ground floor
questions.note: France counts floors the British way: the ground floor is 'le rez-de-chaussée', so 'premier étage' is the British first floor.

questions.question: Three of these countries share a land border with mainland France. Which is the odd one out?
questions.note: Belgium, Spain and Italy are three of mainland France's eight neighbours. Portugal's only land neighbour is Spain.

questions.question: In which year was Britain's National Health Service, the NHS, launched?
questions.note: Aneurin Bevan launched the NHS on 5 July 1948, making Britain the first western country to offer free medical care to its whole population.

questions.question: Put these four art movements in chronological order, earliest first.
questions.note: Standard datings run Neoclassicism from about 1750, Romanticism from about 1780, Impressionism from about 1870 and Cubism from 1907.

questions.question: The letters HP on a bottle of HP Sauce stand for the name of which London landmark?
questions.note: HP stands for Houses of Parliament, which is why the building has appeared on the label since 1903.

questions.question: Until 2019 the kilogram was defined by a platinum-iridium cylinder nicknamed 'Le Grand K', locked in a vault on the outskirts of which capital city?
questions.note: It sits under bell jars in the basement vault at Sèvres, just outside Paris, opened only with three separately held keys.

questions.question: Which British director directed Russell Crowe in both Gladiator (2000) and Robin Hood (2010)?
questions.note: Ridley Scott, born in South Shields in the north-east of England, directed Crowe in Gladiator and again in Robin Hood.

questions.question: France's longest land border is with which country?
questions.note: French Guiana gives France a 730 km border with Brazil — longer than its 623 km border with Spain.

questions.question: Badminton is named after a stately home in which English county?
questions.note: The sport took its name from Badminton House, the Duke of Beaufort's home, where an early version was played in the 1860s.

questions.question: Whistler's Mother, painted in London in 1871, has belonged to the French state since 1891 — which Paris museum displays it today?
questions.note: Officially titled Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1, it moved to the Musée d'Orsay when the former railway station opened as a museum in 1986.
